SETTING THE COMPASS
Course Objectives
1
Think and Work Like an Auditor
Translate frameworks into real audit findings — draft RFIs, evaluate evidence, judge control design vs. operating effectiveness.
2
Master HK's Regulatory Terrain
Navigate PDPO, Cap. 653, GL20, C-RAF 2.0 — and place it against the global frameworks that inform it.
3
Operate in GRC and Technical Worlds
Move fluently between governance/compliance thinking and the technical detail beneath it — one skill, not two.
4
Read the Frontier, Not Just the Established
Apply the same audit judgment to AI governance, crypto-asset regulation, and cloud compliance-as-code.
5
Build a Portfolio, Not Just Sit an Exam
Leave with a semester's worth of applied deliverables — workpapers, control mappings, a capstone case study.

THE RELEVANCE OF INDUSTRY VIEWS
Why This Course Leans on Industry
Audit and compliance is a practiced craft, not a memorized one. Theory tells you what a control should look like; a practitioner tells you what actually happens when it doesn't.
Almost every week this semester hands the floor to someone doing this work right now — CISOs, regulators, SOC leads, Big Four advisors — alongside structured lecture content.

HOW YOU'LL BE ASSESSED
Assessment Weighting

The Group Case Study (Week 13) sits alongside the Exam — it does not replace it.

CS5292 · Week 1 · Before the Frameworks
Prof. Jason Lee
12 / 33
CAUSE, THEN EFFECT
The Incidents That Forced the Issue
JUN
2005
CardSystems Solutions
~40 million card numbers exposed — six months after PCI DSS v1.0 shipped.
→ FRAMEWORK RESPONSE
Proved PCI DSS was needed on day one, not a paperwork exercise.
NOV
2013
Target Corporation
~40 million card numbers and 70 million customer records exposed in-store.
→ FRAMEWORK RESPONSE
Sharpened the US executive order that becomes NIST CSF 1.0 three months later.
FEB
2016
Bangladesh Bank / SWIFT
US$81 million stolen via forged SWIFT transfers (Lazarus Group).
→ FRAMEWORK RESPONSE
HKMA launches CFI / C-RAF 1.0 just ten months later.
DEC
2020
SolarWinds
Trojanized software update reaches ~18,000 organizations worldwide.
→ FRAMEWORK RESPONSE
Sharpens EU focus on third-party ICT risk — feeds directly into DORA.
A deliberately small sample, not a complete list — each has a clean, well-documented line to a framework already on this tour.

GROUNDING THE TIMELINE
Why This Isn't Just Theory
~10,000
patient records on a lost
USB flash drive
6 MAY 2008
Prince of Wales Hospital,
Hospital Authority
A staff member lost a USB flash drive holding working documents with patients' names, HKID numbers, and laboratory test items — and couldn't confirm the data had been deleted per protocol.
Prince of Wales Hospital notified the police and the Privacy Commissioner immediately; no evidence of actual misuse was found at the time.
PDPO had already existed for over a decade by 2008 — this is the kind of ordinary, low-tech incident that turned data protection into a practitioner's discipline in Hong Kong.
We'll go deeper on PCPD's approach — and a full case study — in Week 3.

A DELIBERATE SELECTION
Why These, and Why Non-Exhaustive
Tonight's deep tour was curated, not the whole map — the table you just saw is the fuller picture, and we'll meet nearly every row on it before Week 13.
The selection reflects two things: what I actually saw and worked on inside a Big Four practice, and what Hong Kong organizations are being measured against today.
From Week 2 onward, this course pivots to a Hong Kong-specific lens — everything global tonight was the map; next week we start walking the terrain.
The terrain keeps shifting: DORA went live in Jan 2025 alongside MiCA and TIBER-EU, and NIS2 is expanding the same discipline across 18 critical sectors.

THE COURSE PHILOSOPHY
Cybersecurity Is Not GRC vs. Technical. It's Both.
1
If you can't move between both worlds at a functional level, you're not ready to operate independently.
2
This course is labeled “Audit and Compliance” — but it's really about the integration of both.
3
Expect technical material woven in throughout. When it goes beyond our class time, you're expected to research, read, or ask.
4
Every framework we study this semester exists to answer one question a technical control alone can't: how do you prove it's working?
